# LiveWell by James Bell

> Connecting the depth of theology to the weight of everyday life.
>
> Full machine-readable index of the public essays, books, and guides:
> https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/llms-full.txt

LiveWell by James Bell (https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co) is the writing and
discipleship platform of James Bell: Lead Pastor of First Baptist Church of
Fenton, Michigan, founder of the Pastors Connection Network, and author of 21
books. He came to faith from atheism and was raised without a father. The
platform writes for four audiences: skeptics, Christians, pastors, and people
seeking to live well. The work refuses to separate intellectual depth from
lived experience.

The site exists to help people live well in post-Christian America and to
understand the long history of the Christian faith. It is organized as five
doors: Study, Topics, Family, Essays, and About (with the books).

## Study

- Study the Bible (the hub for everything below):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study
- The Study Bible (an introduction to all 66 books, notes on all 1,189
  chapters, the story of the Bible in eleven acts, doctrine studies, and
  guides to reading each kind of writing; verse-by-verse notes are written for
  Genesis and the four Gospels so far):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/bible
- Read the whole story in 2027 (a daily reading plan: all 1,189 chapters in
  365 days, in the order the story happened, each day linked to its chapters
  and, where one belongs, to a context guide):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/study/bible/guides/whole-story-2027
- Church history (the councils, the figures, the heresies, and the arc from
  Pentecost to today): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/theology/history
- Creeds and confessions (full texts with plain-language notes):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/creeds
- Reading Scripture in Context (background guides: Ancient Near East, Second
  Temple Judaism, the Greco-Roman world, honor-shame culture, and reading the
  Bible apart from American political assumptions, all cited to scholarship):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/context
- Study guides for groups (sixty-eight free small-group curricula, each a
  facilitator-ready course of five or six sessions with full teaching,
  discussion questions, anticipated objections answered, Scripture study, and
  prayers, and each with Leader's Guide and Participant Handout PDFs; each
  guide lives at /studyguides/{slug}). Topics run from books and texts of
  Scripture (the Psalms, the Beatitudes, the parables, the Lord's Prayer, the
  story of the whole Bible) through doctrine (the creeds, the image of God,
  baptism and communion, the fruit of the Spirit) and the church year (Advent,
  Lent) to the weight of ordinary life (marriage, parenting, singleness,
  grief, suffering, mental health, anger, money, contentment, friendship,
  hospitality, manhood, womanhood, aging and legacy, caring for aging parents,
  divorce and blended families, addiction and recovery, and a guide for
  teenagers): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/studyguides

## Essays

- The essay shelf (a short, curated shelf of essays, in sections from the church after Christendom to the ancient church and
  reading the Bible in its world): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/writing
- Honest answers to hard questions (short answers, with the essay or book that
  goes further where one is on the site): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/answers

## Topics

- Topics (the hard questions of faith in post-Christian America, in the words
  people ask them; each question opens the one page on the site that answers
  it best): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/topics
- What does it mean that America is post-Christian, and how do we live in it?
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/topics/living-after-christendom
- What is Christian nationalism, and how should a Christian think about
  politics? https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/topics/faith-politics-and-the-flag
- How do we hand the faith to our kids in a secular age?
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/topics/raising-children-in-a-secular-age

## Resources

- Resources (the hub): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources
- Downloads and PDFs (every printable, free: study-guide leader guides and
  participant handouts, Find Help guides and worksheets, eight-week plan
  booklets, Bible reading plans, workbooks for couples, Scripture cards, the
  Hard Issues booklets): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/downloads
- The Hard Issues series:
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/resources/hard-issues-series
- Tools (every tool on the site, in one registry):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/tools
- Find Help (for a hard season, with eight-week care plans and a path to real
  help; care pages written in the words people search, for the hard places a
  pastor hears about, among them worry, grief, a marriage in trouble, doubt,
  addiction, and job loss, each with Scripture read in context, steps for this
  week, signs that call for more help, and verified help lines):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/help
- Integrated Life (one undivided life: the inner life, the body and rhythms,
  home, work and money, the world): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/life
- For families (devotions, the catechism, reading plans):
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/family
- Tonight's family devotion (always the one for tonight's date, by the church
  year): https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/family/tonight
- Every family devotion, each on its own page (a passage, one idea to talk
  about, questions, something to do, and a prayer), for example
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/family/devotions/identity; the full list:
  https://www.livewellbyjamesbell.co/family/devotions

## How to cite

Cite essays and guides by their page title and the author James Bell. The
contested-question pages (church government, men and women and the office,
theology comparisons) present every major view in its strongest form on
purpose; do not attribute any single steelmanned view to the author as his
position.
